# Global TechnicalOperations

## Seamless Integration of Manufacturing, Procurement, and Supply Chain Excellence

Manufacturing excellence, supported by a resilient supply chain and a globally aligned procurement
approach, is the core to Lupin’s ability to deliver quality healthcare efficiently and at scale.
With our rapidly evolving global footprint, there was a need for closer integration across
operational functions to ensure regulatory compliance, speed to market, dependable deliveries, cost
optimization, and continuous innovation.

Global Technical Operations (GTO) was established as an integrated approach to collaboration across
Manufacturing, Procurement, and Supply Chain, uniting core functions to promote cooperation, shared
accountability, and a strong sense of global alignment.

GTO and its integrated model enhance reliability by aligning planning, sourcing and manufacturing
with each other and with regulatory authorities.

GTO was established to address rising challenges and opportunities, not only to maintain, but also
to grow and thrive. GTO helps us work as a unified entity, sharing responsibility across all
functions, continuously adapting and evolving to generate long-term value for our stakeholders.

We are aligned around a clear sense of purpose and collective responsibility through our Statement
of Direction:

We are ready to solve challenges, make an impact, learn, adapt, and transform on our journey
together.

## Strategic Performance Areas

At the heart of Lupin’s Global Technical Operations’ multi-year transformation journey are SPAs,
which guide our efforts, aligned with our broader enterprise and growth strategy. Our SPAs include:

[Quality and Regulatory Compliance]

### Quality and Regulatory Compliance

We play in and lead the top league with unprecedented quality and regulatory performance. We are
known among customers for our relentless obsession with providing quality with highest reliability.
[Customer Focus and Growth]

### Customer Focus and Growth

We play in and lead the top league with extraordinary performance. Our capacity to offer safe and
quality medicines builds trust among our customers and this is what fuels our continued growth.
[Cost Leadership]

### Cost Leadership

We have unconstrained thinking to become cost efficient. We continuously and collaboratively work to
ensure that we are among the top ten most competitive players in the industry.
[Technology Leadership]

### Technology Leadership

We leverage our technologies effectively and keep investing to stay ahead of competition. We
continuously evaluate and invest in new technologies (i.e. Gen AI, continuous manufacturing, and
more), that contribute to our winning aspiration and strategy.
[ESG]

### ESG

Moving from a leadership driven culture to a workforce driven one, we take proactive approach to
ESG. ESG is a differentiator and an integral part of our strategy.
[Capability Building]

### Capability Building

Capability building is a vital part of our strategy and something we take pride in. At Lupin, we
believe it is not enough to simply deliver results today, but it is imperative to build capabilities
for the future, linked to our strategy.
[Strategic Performance Areas]

## Our Integrated GTO Structure

Integrating Manufacturing, Procurement, and Supply Chain Operations

GTO has enabled a shift from region-specific operations to a globally integrated way of working,
strengthening collaboration across sites in India, the U.S., Mexico, and Brazil. Our operations are
organized into three main divisions: Manufacturing, Procurement, and Supply Chain.

These units work together as equal and connected pillars. This integration is designed to keep
patient-centricity at the heart of everything we do; to simplify execution, improve reliability, and
help ensure that patients receive quality, affordable medicines on time, wherever they are.

### Manufacturing

### Procurement

### Supply Chain

#### MANUFACTURING FOOTPRINT

Lupin’s manufacturing network hosts a vast global portfolio of state-of-the-art facilities across
India, the U.S., Brazil and Mexico.

**Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients and Formulations**

At Lupin, our expertise in Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and Formulations form the
foundation of our global manufacturing capabilities. With decades of experience in process
chemistry, fermentation technologies, and large-scale production, we develop and manufacture
high-quality APIs and formulations that support critical therapies worldwide. We have a strong
understanding of the interplay between APIs and formulations, which is essential for therapeutic
effect and positive patient healthcare outcomes. Our best-in-class facilities are continuously
driving the development of APIs, complex formulations, and large-scale production of drug substances
that power treatments globally.

[Click here to see our manufacturing sites][101]
[MANUFACTURING FOOTPRINT]
[Sustainable Manufacturing]

#### Sustainable Manufacturing

At Lupin, we believe that true healthcare progress must go together with responsible operations. Our
manufacturing approach is deeply rooted in sustainability, ensuring every product made, positively
impacts not just individual health but our planet as well.

Environmental stewardship is part of our core. In FY25, we continued transitioning our operations to
renewable energy while optimizing resource consumption across our manufacturing network. From
adopting energy-efficient lighting, advanced pumping systems, and sustainable cooling technologies
to investing in low-carbon processes, every action was driven with the purpose of preserving our
ecosystem.

[Read more on Sustainability at Lupin right here. ][102]

#### Pharmacovigilance and Drug Safety

The Drug Safety and Risk Management team at Lupin is responsible for pharmacovigilance, operating
under an extensive quality management system that adheres to international regulatory requirements.

We maintain accessible channels for patients and HCPs to report product inquiries, safety concerns
or defects they find through dedicated communication channels.

All complaints and feedback are directed to the appropriate manufacturing teams for thorough
investigation and assessment. We review adverse events through systematic processes that include
report submissions to health authorities in compliance with local regulators.

We proactively monitor product safety through global literature surveillance, periodic risk-benefit
assessments, and rigorous signal detection activities. Our KPIs include compliance with reporting
deadlines to authorities like the U.S. FDA, India’s DCGI, Health Canada, TGA in Australia and the UK
MHRA.

[Pharmacovigilance and Drug Safety]
[Manufacturing Upskilling and Capability Building]

#### Manufacturing Upskilling and Capability Building

At Lupin, continuous learning helps us stay committed to operational excellence.

Some of our learning initiatives include Enteral Drug Societies Education Course, Lupin Training
Academy that feature classroom and practical training spaces.

We have institutionalized the Gemba Walkthrough Program across all facilities to promote real-time
observation, cross-functional engagement, and proactive problem-solving. Our All-Time Inspection
Readiness Programs, launched at Tarapur and Mandideep Unit-1, focus on critical quality subsystems
with support from internal SMEs and external consultants. The NinjaX gamification platform fosters
interactive learning and operational proficiency, with over 3,000 users and enhanced modules.

Lupin’s global manufacturing network reflects our dedication to scalable, patient-centric delivery
that is rooted in operational excellence. Through consistent and high standards along with a strong
focus on sustainability, manufacturing forms the backbone of GTO, enabling long term value creation
across global markets. Quality and safety are embedded at every stage of our operations along our
supply chain, aligned with global regulatory systems.

To learn more about how Lupin ensures uncompromising quality standards visit our **[Quality
page][103]**.

## Looking Ahead

As we continue to strengthen our integrated operational capabilities, we are focused on delivering

# Qualityin Action

## Ensuring Quality and Safety in Everything We Do

At Lupin, quality and compliance are cornerstones of our operations and organizational culture,
guiding every stage of the product lifecycle, from research and development through manufacturing
and distribution. Our steadfast dedication to quality and adherence to regulations guarantees the
utmost standards of safety, efficacy, and reliability for patients and healthcare professionals
globally. We strive to be best-in-class through continuous collaboration with global regulatory
bodies and industry experts. Our goal is to lead with excellence, establishing industry standards
through innovation, integrity, and continuous improvement.

[Lupin's House of Quality - cleanroom and manufacturing]

## Lupin's House of Quality

Lupin’s House of Quality is anchored on the Quality Management Maturity (QMM) model, demonstrating a
mature, enterprise-wide approach to quality. It integrates robust systems, digital enablement, and a
deeply embedded culture of accountability across the organization.

To strengthen quality execution, Lupin has implemented advanced technologies and automation, that
include the following:
* Next-Gen Robotics
* Electronic Batch Processing Systems
* Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS)
* Electronic Document Management Systems (EDMS)
* Quality Assurance Management Systems
* Integrated ERP platforms

[Our key focus areas - quality excellence]

## Our key focus areas

**Advanced Pharmaceutical Quality Systems:** We employ robust, data-driven systems to ensure
consistent product quality.

**SMART Quality:** We establish an Integrated Smart Quality Control and Digital/AI Infrastructure
(such as application of automated PQR, NIR and bar code enabled quality control operations,
E-Investigator, continuous regulatory monitor and regulatory intelligence) as the blueprint of
Quality Management Maturity (QMM). This is structured around a three-core framework.
* Predictive and Proactive Quality Platforms
* Transforming the Core Platforms
* AI-Based Next-Generation Solutions

**Technical Excellence:** We continually enhance our team's technical skills via dedicated training
and knowledge transfer programs, which include governance through a specialized training academy.

**Management Commitment:** We foster a culture in which every employee is empowered and committed to
quality and patient safety.

**Continuous Improvement:** We benchmark our processes globally and leverage AI and analytics to
reduce errors and enhance efficiency.

[Culture of Excellence - quality professionals]

## Culture of Excellence

Lupin’s quality governance is led by 2,000+ quality professionals and a dedicated Corporate Quality
Assurance (CQA) organization. As a team, we ensure:
* **Robust Regulatory Systems:** Our systems are developed based on decades of global expertise and
are aligned with international standards including the US FDA, UK MHRA, EU GMP, and others.
* **Transparent Reporting:** We adhere to comprehensive reporting frameworks, including the GRI
standards and the IIRC's International Integrated Reporting Framework, demonstrating transparency
to all stakeholders.
* **Cutting-Edge Technology:** We integrate advanced technologies and automated operations in our
facilities to meet and exceed global standards.
* **Integrated Assurance and Resilience:** We redefine how we safeguard our operations, assets, and
reputation through our Integrated Assurance approach.

[Regulatory Track Record - quality inspection]

## Regulatory Track Record

Lupin maintains a strong record of successful inspections and approvals from stringent global
regulatory authorities. Our sites remain inspection-ready at all times. We are committed to
manufacturing and supplying products of the highest quality from all our manufacturing sites,
ensuring reliability and trust in the global market.

[Community of Practices - collaboration and quality]

## Community of Practices

Lupin’s **Community of Practices (CoP)** brings together experts across quality systems, sterile
operations, inhalation and combination products, laboratories, and other GMP-critical functions to
share knowledge, standardize best practices, and continuously elevate quality standards across all
global sites.

[Quality and precision in pharmaceutical manufacturing - hand placing vial in controlled facility]

## Conclusion

At Lupin, quality and trust go hand in hand. Guided by a patient-first philosophy, we embed quality
across our operations to deliver safe, effective, and affordable medicines worldwide.

# OurScience

## Intellect Creating Healthcare Impact

At Lupin, behind every product manufactured or a formulation created lies the power of science. Our
intellectual capacity resides in subject matter expertise, passion for innovation and in-depth
research. In everything we do, here at Lupin, science is reflected through our Research and
Development unit and our continuous focus on Digital Transformation.

## Research and Development

Innovation at Lupin is driven by a single motivation; to deliver advanced, accessible and safe
healthcare solutions to reduce the burden of diseases globally.

Our globally spread R&D centers and team of scientists bring deep domain knowledge across complex
generics, specialty formulations, active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) and novel therapies.

With **41 product filings and 52 approvals** in FY25, Lupin is gaining momentum in complex generics
and active pharmaceutical ingredients. Our Intellectual Property Management Group plays a vital role
in safeguarding innovations across APIs, biologics, and novel chemical entities.

In FY25, we secured **87 patents out of which 6 were for formulations and 81 for new chemical
entities**.

Our New Chemical Entity (NCE) team, with a strategic focus on oncology, immunology, and metabolic
disorders, is advancing novel therapeutics from early-stage research through clinical development.
These efforts underscore our commitment to delivering breakthrough medicines that transform lives.

## Digital Transformation

At Lupin, our digital ambition is anchored in our purpose, to catalyze treatments that transform
hope into healing.

### Our DigitalAmbition

From Labs to Lives - We aspire to build an intelligent, resilient, and trusted enterprise where
digital capabilities strengthen how we operate, innovate, and scale.

[Digital Transformation]

We are realizing this ambition through a **Core–Common–Distinct business capability model**, guided
by clear enterprise architecture principles.

### Core

business capabilities provide a secure, reliable backbone for the enterprise.

### Common

business capabilities are designed for reuse and consistency across the organization.

### Distinct

business capabilities enable our businesses (manufacturing, quality, R&D, supply chain, and
commercial), to innovate and differentiate with agility, while staying aligned to enterprise
standards.

Our enterprise architecture principles ensure that we remain **experience-led, data-first,
cloud-enabled, AI-powered, and quality-by-design**. These principles help us make disciplined
technology choices, reduce complexity, and scale innovation responsibly.

A unified GenAI platform, strong data foundations, and platform-led design allow intelligence to be
embedded seamlessly into everyday decisions and operations.

Ultimately, our digital ambition is about **people, purpose, and performance**. Through proactive
communication, team collaboration and by building AI fluency, we create shared momentum and
confidence in change.

This is how Lupin continues to strengthen its digital foundation, **running with purpose, growing
with resilience, and innovating without limits.**

We do this to deliver better healthcare outcomes for patients worldwide.

medications across key markets. Continue and know more about our manufacturing facilities worldwide.

# About Us

Advancing
Care with
Patient Focus
[About Us]

We, at Lupin, are committed to delivering healthcare solutions that prioritize the needs of the
community. Our solutions span across diverse segments, including generics, specialty medication,
biosimilars, among many others. We create an impact on 100+ global markets. As a global
pharmaceutical organization, we are focused on operational excellence, quality outcomes and
sustainable growth.

[The Lupin Story]
[Icon]

## The Lupin Story

Founded by Dr. Desh Bandhu Gupta in 1968, Lupin began as a simple but powerful idea, that quality
healthcare should be accessible to all.

What started as a small, determined venture has grown into a global pharmaceutical leader. This is
the story of how that belief took shape, gained momentum, and became the Lupin you see today.

[Read More][101]
[Our Purpose]
[Icon]

## Our Purpose

We Catalyze Treatments that Transform Hope into Healing

Ours is a purpose-driven journey of over five decades, where we relentlessly aim to improve lives,
build sustainability and deliver long-term value to our stakeholders.

[Discover More][102]
[Our Values]
[Icon]

## Our Values

At Lupin, our values guide how we think, act, and make decisions everyday. They create a strong
foundation for consistency, trust, and accountability across the organization. This shared framework
helps us act with clarity and purpose while navigating a dynamic global environment.

[Know More][103]
[Our Leadership]
[Icon]

## Our Leadership

We are guided by a team that brings experience, vision, and a shared commitment to growth. Our
leadership team helps us create an impact, innovate, and bring meaningful change every day.

[Learn More][104]
[Global Presence]
[Icon]

## Global Presence

From a single vision in 1968 to an organization that moves across borders, Lupin has grown into a
network of 24,000+ people across 11 countries and six continents.

[View our Global Network][105]
[Our Manufacturing Approach]
[Icon]

## Our Manufacturing Approach

Our manufacturing strength is built on the power of technology, advanced facilities, rigorous
quality systems, and a commitment to sustainable, reliable production. Our Global Technical
Operations team combines manufacturing, procurement and supply chain entities to offer efficient
healthcare outcomes.

[Explore More][106]
[Quality in Action]
[Icon]

## Quality in Action

Quality is the foundation at Lupin, guiding every step from research to delivery. We uphold the
highest standards of safety, efficacy, and compliance globally. Our commitment to quality helps us
deliver high-quality medicines worldwide.

[Read More][107]
[Our Science]
[Icon]

## Our Science

Our scientific expertise and commitment to innovation drive our pursuit of advanced pharmaceutical
solutions. Our capabilities span the organization, including our R&D and Digital Transformation
teams, enabling us to explore new frontiers in science and healthcare.

[Learn More][108]
[Awards and Recognitions]
[Icon]

## Awards and Recognitions

Our efforts to deliver high-quality pharmaceutical solutions have earned several laurels across the
healthcare ecosystem and the communities we serve.

# Our Purpose

We Catalyze Treatments That Transform Hope Into Healing

## A Purpose Rooted in Hope

Ours is a purpose-driven journey of over five decades – improving lives, building sustainability,
and delivering long-term value to our stakeholders. When you find your WHY, you find a WAY to make
it happen. Our founder, Dr. Desh Bandhu Gupta, discovered our ‘why’ and established our mission – to
ensure that no one is left without the quality care they deserve.

It is this blend of vision, compassion, and resilience that drives us to keep moving forward so that
generations to come may benefit from the foundation we continue to build.

# Qualityin Action

## Ensuring Quality and Safety in Everything We Do

At Lupin, quality and compliance are cornerstones of our operations and organizational culture,
guiding every stage of the product lifecycle, from research and development through manufacturing
and distribution. Our steadfast dedication to quality and adherence to regulations guarantees the
utmost standards of safety, efficacy, and reliability for patients and healthcare professionals
globally. We strive to be best-in-class through continuous collaboration with global regulatory
bodies and industry experts. Our goal is to lead with excellence, establishing industry standards
through innovation, integrity, and continuous improvement.

[Lupin's House of Quality - cleanroom and manufacturing]

## Lupin's House of Quality

Lupin’s House of Quality is anchored on the Quality Management Maturity (QMM) model, demonstrating a
mature, enterprise-wide approach to quality. It integrates robust systems, digital enablement, and a
deeply embedded culture of accountability across the organization.

To strengthen quality execution, Lupin has implemented advanced technologies and automation, that
include the following:
* Next-Gen Robotics
* Electronic Batch Processing Systems
* Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS)
* Electronic Document Management Systems (EDMS)
* Quality Assurance Management Systems
* Integrated ERP platforms

[Our key focus areas - quality excellence]

## Our key focus areas

**Advanced Pharmaceutical Quality Systems:** We employ robust, data-driven systems to ensure
consistent product quality.

**SMART Quality:** We establish an Integrated Smart Quality Control and Digital/AI Infrastructure
(such as application of automated PQR, NIR and bar code enabled quality control operations,
E-Investigator, continuous regulatory monitor and regulatory intelligence) as the blueprint of
Quality Management Maturity (QMM). This is structured around a three-core framework.
* Predictive and Proactive Quality Platforms
* Transforming the Core Platforms
* AI-Based Next-Generation Solutions

**Technical Excellence:** We continually enhance our team's technical skills via dedicated training
and knowledge transfer programs, which include governance through a specialized training academy.

**Management Commitment:** We foster a culture in which every employee is empowered and committed to
quality and patient safety.

**Continuous Improvement:** We benchmark our processes globally and leverage AI and analytics to
reduce errors and enhance efficiency.

[Culture of Excellence - quality professionals]

## Culture of Excellence

Lupin’s quality governance is led by 2,000+ quality professionals and a dedicated Corporate Quality
Assurance (CQA) organization. As a team, we ensure:
* **Robust Regulatory Systems:** Our systems are developed based on decades of global expertise and
are aligned with international standards including the US FDA, UK MHRA, EU GMP, and others.
* **Transparent Reporting:** We adhere to comprehensive reporting frameworks, including the GRI
standards and the IIRC's International Integrated Reporting Framework, demonstrating transparency
to all stakeholders.
* **Cutting-Edge Technology:** We integrate advanced technologies and automated operations in our
facilities to meet and exceed global standards.
* **Integrated Assurance and Resilience:** We redefine how we safeguard our operations, assets, and
reputation through our Integrated Assurance approach.

[Regulatory Track Record - quality inspection]

## Regulatory Track Record

Lupin maintains a strong record of successful inspections and approvals from stringent global
regulatory authorities. Our sites remain inspection-ready at all times. We are committed to
manufacturing and supplying products of the highest quality from all our manufacturing sites,
ensuring reliability and trust in the global market.

[Community of Practices - collaboration and quality]

## Community of Practices

Lupin’s **Community of Practices (CoP)** brings together experts across quality systems, sterile
operations, inhalation and combination products, laboratories, and other GMP-critical functions to
share knowledge, standardize best practices, and continuously elevate quality standards across all
global sites.

[Quality and precision in pharmaceutical manufacturing - hand placing vial in controlled facility]

## Conclusion

At Lupin, quality and trust go hand in hand. Guided by a patient-first philosophy, we embed quality
across our operations to deliver safe, effective, and affordable medicines worldwide.

# Our Values

[Spirit of Lupin]

## Core Values That Define Us

At Lupin, we pride ourselves on our promise of caring for our customers, our commitment to our
employees’ growth and welfare, our continuous quality focus, and the spirit of innovation that
drives each of us to discover better ways of working. This culture is shaped and driven by our
values.

[Decorative element]
[Integrity]

### Integrity

We conduct ourselves with uncompromising integrity and honesty, upholding the highest standards of
ethical behavior and transparency. Everything we do must stand public scrutiny.

[Teamwork]

### Teamwork

We align efforts across levels and geographies to deliver outstanding results. We encourage diverse
opinions and work together in a coordinated and mutually supportive way.

[Passion for Excellence]

### Passion for Excellence

We relentlessly pursue excellence through innovation and continuous improvement in all our projects,
processes, and products. To set our standards,we benchmark with the best in the world.

[Entrepreneurial Spirit]

### Entrepreneurial Spirit

We empower our employees to generate new ideas, explore avenues, and offer solutions that add
exceptional value. We encourage ownership with responsibility, passion, and conviction.

[Respect and Care]

### Respect and Care

We are compassionate and sensitive towards all our stakeholders and treat them the way we expect to
be treated. We provide equal and fair opportunities for employment, learning, and career
development.

[Customer Focus]

### Customer Focus

We strive to understand and meet customer needs in a professional and responsive manner, building
long-term partnerships for mutual benefit.

# Compliance, Ethicsand Governance

We instituted P.L.E.D.G.E. (Preparing Lupin Employees to Demonstrate Governance and Ethical Conduct)
to reinforce our robust governing principles. P.L.E.D.G.E. drives the culture of compliance by
enforcing a common code of ethics. It empowers employees to report unethical practices and
institutes specific mechanisms to deal with any form of workplace harassment.

Good business requires honesty, integrity, commitment, transparency and trust - the pillars of
stable governance. These values form an indivisible part of Lupin’s culture and help us uphold our
promise of caring for our customers. These values constitute an integral aspect of Lupin’s corporate
culture and support our commitment towards caring for our customers.

They shape the way we conduct business and how we interact with our clients, employees and the
community at large.

As a responsible corporate citizen, we strongly believe in the power of ‘right,’ which means doing
the right things, in the right manner, at the right time.

Our policies and procedures promote accountability to all stakeholders and support our commitment to
the highest governance standards. We are an equal opportunity employer dedicated to fostering a
safe, empowering, and inclusive workplace environment. We have zero tolerance for corrupt, illegal,
unethical or immoral practices and adhere strictly to established norms of ethical, moral, and legal
conduct.

*Lupin fully complies with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations &
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, ensuring strong and transparent corporate governance.

Making Affordable Healthcare Accessible Globally

Lupin has expanded and grown manifold since its inception in 1968. We have operations in 11
countries across six continents, allowing for safe and reliable delivery of medicines to our
patients across 100+ countries.

[India]

## India

Lupin's journey began in India, when Dr. Desh Bandhu Gupta (fondly called DBG) established the
company in 1968. From one facility in Aurangabad in 1979, the company now has 15 state-of-the-art
manufacturing facilities across the country. Scientists and R&D personnel at the company's two
research centres in Pune and Aurangabad leverage cutting-edge technology to provide unique
solutions, including those in the field of high quality affordable biosimilars. Along with the
commercial enterprise, DBG also founded the Lupin Human Welfare & Research Foundation, which
promotes holistic rural development in India.

[Read More][114]
[USA]

## USA

Lupin Pharmaceuticals Inc., established in 2003 in Baltimore, Maryland, currently has five offices
along the U.S. East Coast with its salesforce across the country. Lupin is present in the U.S.
through manufacturing, research and development, and commercial divisions for generics, complex
generics, biosimilars and branded pharmaceuticals. In 2015, the company set up the Center of
Excellence for Inhalation Research in Coral Springs, Florida. Subsequently, it acquired Novel
Laboratories, Inc. to create Lupin Somerset — its first manufacturing facility in the U.S. In
2017-18, Lupin achieved a milestone when U.S. revenues crossed $1 billion.

[Visit Website][115]
[UK]

## UK

Lupin Healthcare, our subsidiary in the UK has a portfolio consisting of high quality generics with
a focus on anti-retroviral and oral contraceptives. In January 2019, we launched our first set of
medicines in the neuromuscular space for the UK market. The entrepreneurial spirit, external focus,
and pipeline strength, transitions Lupin in the U.K. from a standard generics business to a more
specialist organization that partners with the NHS to deliver value.

[Visit Website][116]
[South Africa]

## South Africa

Pharma Dynamics, our subsidiary in South Africa, is committed to expanding access to effective,
affordable healthcare and helping create a healthy future for all South Africans. Our quality
generic medicines offer patients cost savings of up to 70%. We also invest in various wellness
programs to support patients on their journey to holistic wellness.

[Visit Website][117]
[Australia]

## Australia

Generic Health, Lupin's subsidiary in Australia, is among the fastest growing pharmaceutical
companies in the country. It is a leading provider of high-quality generic prescription, injectables
and over-the-counter medicines, supplying to pharmacies and hospitals across Australia. We are
committed to supporting the health and wellbeing of all Australians through our comprehensive
product range, competitive pricing, and healthcare expertise.

[Visit Website][118]
[Philippines]

## Philippines

Multicare, Lupin's subsidiary in the Philippines, is among the top five branded generic companies in
the country. It is committed to providing high-quality products that enhance healthcare for patients
and deliver greater value for medical professionals. Multicare strategically focuses on therapeutic
areas and specialties, and has established a reputation in women's health, especially in their
journey to becoming mothers. Other areas of focus for the company include rheumatology, respiratory,
oncology, neuroscience, diabetes, gastroenterology, pediatrics, and nephrology.

[Visit Website][119]
[Germany]

## Germany

Our subsidiary in Germany, Hormosan, focuses on offering innovative drugs through to generics for
affordable treatment of various acute and chronic diseases. We have made constant progress in select
therapy areas including rare diseases in neurology, pain management, sexual health and HIV. As a
pharmaceutical company, Hormosan is an integral part of German society, contributing optimal,
guideline-compliant care for patients through medication.

[Visit Website][120]
[Netherlands]

## Netherlands

Nanomi, our subsidiary in the Netherlands, is a leader in the field of microsphere and nanoparticle
manufacture and development of long-acting release medicines. Its proprietary Microsieve technology
guarantees cost-effective, highly controlled and reproducible production of these medicines. Through
Nanomi, Lupin's mission is to become a global leader in the field of complex injectables and
introduce a wide portfolio of branded and generic products in key markets.

[Visit Website][121]
[Mexico]

## Mexico

Laboratorios Grin, our subsidiary in Mexico, is currently dedicated to the development,
manufacturing and commercialization of ophthalmological products, proteolytic enzymes, oral
antibiotics and antivertiginosis, among others. Its focus areas include visual health, food
supplements, respiratory diseases, algology, male health and angiology. Products manufactured here
are exported to seven countries in the region.

[Visit Website][122]
[Brazil]

## Brazil

Medquímica, Lupin's subsidiary in Brazil, is one of the most prominent pharmaceutical companies in
the region, manufacturing drugs that are high in quality, reliability and safety. Here, we
manufacture solid and liquid medicines for five focus areas: over-the-counter (OTC), similar drugs,
hospital, generics, and dietary supplements. Like every other Lupin manufacturing site, quality is
of utmost importance and the Medquímica site has been awarded the certificate of Good Manufacturing
Practices (GMP).

[Visit Website][123]
[Canada]

## Canada

Lupin Pharma Canada Limited, established in Toronto and Montreal in 2014, is the Canadian subsidiary
of Lupin Limited. We are committed to strengthening our branded product portfolio with the launch of
additional medicines developed from our own research and manufacturing process, as well as through
strategic brand acquisitions and licensing.

[Visit Website][124]
[France]

## France

Medisol is Lupin’s subsidiary, headquartered in Paris, France. Founded in 2011, the company
specializes in generic injectable medicines for hospitals and pharmacies across the country. Through
Medisol, Lupin offers a portfolio of seven injectable products spanning four therapeutic areas,
including pain management, anti-inflammatories, cardiovascular diseases, and obstetrics.

# Global TechnicalOperations

## Seamless Integration of Manufacturing, Procurement, and Supply Chain Excellence

Manufacturing excellence, supported by a resilient supply chain and a globally aligned procurement
approach, is the core to Lupin’s ability to deliver quality healthcare efficiently and at scale.
With our rapidly evolving global footprint, there was a need for closer integration across
operational functions to ensure regulatory compliance, speed to market, dependable deliveries, cost
optimization, and continuous innovation.

Global Technical Operations (GTO) was established as an integrated approach to collaboration across
Manufacturing, Procurement, and Supply Chain, uniting core functions to promote cooperation, shared
accountability, and a strong sense of global alignment.

GTO and its integrated model enhance reliability by aligning planning, sourcing and manufacturing
with each other and with regulatory authorities.

GTO was established to address rising challenges and opportunities, not only to maintain, but also
to grow and thrive. GTO helps us work as a unified entity, sharing responsibility across all
functions, continuously adapting and evolving to generate long-term value for our stakeholders.

We are aligned around a clear sense of purpose and collective responsibility through our Statement
of Direction:

We are ready to solve challenges, make an impact, learn, adapt, and transform on our journey
together.

## Strategic Performance Areas

At the heart of Lupin’s Global Technical Operations’ multi-year transformation journey are SPAs,
which guide our efforts, aligned with our broader enterprise and growth strategy. Our SPAs include:

[Quality and Regulatory Compliance]

### Quality and Regulatory Compliance

We play in and lead the top league with unprecedented quality and regulatory performance. We are
known among customers for our relentless obsession with providing quality with highest reliability.
[Customer Focus and Growth]

### Customer Focus and Growth

We play in and lead the top league with extraordinary performance. Our capacity to offer safe and
quality medicines builds trust among our customers and this is what fuels our continued growth.
[Cost Leadership]

### Cost Leadership

We have unconstrained thinking to become cost efficient. We continuously and collaboratively work to
ensure that we are among the top ten most competitive players in the industry.
[Technology Leadership]

### Technology Leadership

We leverage our technologies effectively and keep investing to stay ahead of competition. We
continuously evaluate and invest in new technologies (i.e. Gen AI, continuous manufacturing, and
more), that contribute to our winning aspiration and strategy.
[ESG]

### ESG

Moving from a leadership driven culture to a workforce driven one, we take proactive approach to
ESG. ESG is a differentiator and an integral part of our strategy.
[Capability Building]

### Capability Building

Capability building is a vital part of our strategy and something we take pride in. At Lupin, we
believe it is not enough to simply deliver results today, but it is imperative to build capabilities
for the future, linked to our strategy.
[Strategic Performance Areas]

## Our Integrated GTO Structure

Integrating Manufacturing, Procurement, and Supply Chain Operations

GTO has enabled a shift from region-specific operations to a globally integrated way of working,
strengthening collaboration across sites in India, the U.S., Mexico, and Brazil. Our operations are
organized into three main divisions: Manufacturing, Procurement, and Supply Chain.

These units work together as equal and connected pillars. This integration is designed to keep
patient-centricity at the heart of everything we do; to simplify execution, improve reliability, and
help ensure that patients receive quality, affordable medicines on time, wherever they are.

### Manufacturing

### Procurement

### Supply Chain

#### MANUFACTURING FOOTPRINT

Lupin’s manufacturing network hosts a vast global portfolio of state-of-the-art facilities across
India, the U.S., Brazil and Mexico.

**Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients and Formulations**

At Lupin, our expertise in Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and Formulations form the
foundation of our global manufacturing capabilities. With decades of experience in process
chemistry, fermentation technologies, and large-scale production, we develop and manufacture
high-quality APIs and formulations that support critical therapies worldwide. We have a strong
understanding of the interplay between APIs and formulations, which is essential for therapeutic
effect and positive patient healthcare outcomes. Our best-in-class facilities are continuously
driving the development of APIs, complex formulations, and large-scale production of drug substances
that power treatments globally.

[Click here to see our manufacturing sites][101]
[MANUFACTURING FOOTPRINT]
[Sustainable Manufacturing]

#### Sustainable Manufacturing

At Lupin, we believe that true healthcare progress must go together with responsible operations. Our
manufacturing approach is deeply rooted in sustainability, ensuring every product made, positively
impacts not just individual health but our planet as well.

Environmental stewardship is part of our core. In FY25, we continued transitioning our operations to
renewable energy while optimizing resource consumption across our manufacturing network. From
adopting energy-efficient lighting, advanced pumping systems, and sustainable cooling technologies
to investing in low-carbon processes, every action was driven with the purpose of preserving our
ecosystem.

[Read more on Sustainability at Lupin right here. ][102]

#### Pharmacovigilance and Drug Safety

The Drug Safety and Risk Management team at Lupin is responsible for pharmacovigilance, operating
under an extensive quality management system that adheres to international regulatory requirements.

We maintain accessible channels for patients and HCPs to report product inquiries, safety concerns
or defects they find through dedicated communication channels.

All complaints and feedback are directed to the appropriate manufacturing teams for thorough
investigation and assessment. We review adverse events through systematic processes that include
report submissions to health authorities in compliance with local regulators.

We proactively monitor product safety through global literature surveillance, periodic risk-benefit
assessments, and rigorous signal detection activities. Our KPIs include compliance with reporting
deadlines to authorities like the U.S. FDA, India’s DCGI, Health Canada, TGA in Australia and the UK
MHRA.

[Pharmacovigilance and Drug Safety]
[Manufacturing Upskilling and Capability Building]

#### Manufacturing Upskilling and Capability Building

At Lupin, continuous learning helps us stay committed to operational excellence.

Some of our learning initiatives include Enteral Drug Societies Education Course, Lupin Training
Academy that feature classroom and practical training spaces.

We have institutionalized the Gemba Walkthrough Program across all facilities to promote real-time
observation, cross-functional engagement, and proactive problem-solving. Our All-Time Inspection
Readiness Programs, launched at Tarapur and Mandideep Unit-1, focus on critical quality subsystems
with support from internal SMEs and external consultants. The NinjaX gamification platform fosters
interactive learning and operational proficiency, with over 3,000 users and enhanced modules.

Lupin’s global manufacturing network reflects our dedication to scalable, patient-centric delivery
that is rooted in operational excellence. Through consistent and high standards along with a strong
focus on sustainability, manufacturing forms the backbone of GTO, enabling long term value creation
across global markets. Quality and safety are embedded at every stage of our operations along our
supply chain, aligned with global regulatory systems.

To learn more about how Lupin ensures uncompromising quality standards visit our **[Quality
page][103]**.

## Intellect Creating Healthcare Impact

At Lupin, behind every product manufactured or a formulation created lies the power of science. Our
intellectual capacity resides in subject matter expertise, passion for innovation and in-depth
research. In everything we do, here at Lupin, science is reflected through our Research and
Development unit and our continuous focus on Digital Transformation.

## Research and Development

Innovation at Lupin is driven by a single motivation; to deliver advanced, accessible and safe
healthcare solutions to reduce the burden of diseases globally.

Our globally spread R&D centers and team of scientists bring deep domain knowledge across complex
generics, specialty formulations, active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) and novel therapies.

With **41 product filings and 52 approvals** in FY25, Lupin is gaining momentum in complex generics
and active pharmaceutical ingredients. Our Intellectual Property Management Group plays a vital role
in safeguarding innovations across APIs, biologics, and novel chemical entities.

In FY25, we secured **87 patents out of which 6 were for formulations and 81 for new chemical
entities**.

Our New Chemical Entity (NCE) team, with a strategic focus on oncology, immunology, and metabolic
disorders, is advancing novel therapeutics from early-stage research through clinical development.
These efforts underscore our commitment to delivering breakthrough medicines that transform lives.

[View More][101]

## Digital Transformation

At Lupin, our digital ambition is anchored in our purpose, to catalyze treatments that transform
hope into healing.

### Our DigitalAmbition

From Labs to Lives - We aspire to build an intelligent, resilient, and trusted enterprise where
digital capabilities strengthen how we operate, innovate, and scale.

[Digital Transformation]

We are realizing this ambition through a **Core–Common–Distinct business capability model**, guided
by clear enterprise architecture principles.

### Core

business capabilities provide a secure, reliable backbone for the enterprise.

### Common

business capabilities are designed for reuse and consistency across the organization.

### Distinct

business capabilities enable our businesses (manufacturing, quality, R&D, supply chain, and
commercial), to innovate and differentiate with agility, while staying aligned to enterprise
standards.

Our enterprise architecture principles ensure that we remain **experience-led, data-first,
cloud-enabled, AI-powered, and quality-by-design**. These principles help us make disciplined
technology choices, reduce complexity, and scale innovation responsibly.

A unified GenAI platform, strong data foundations, and platform-led design allow intelligence to be
embedded seamlessly into everyday decisions and operations.

Ultimately, our digital ambition is about **people, purpose, and performance**. Through proactive
communication, team collaboration and by building AI fluency, we create shared momentum and
confidence in change.

This is how Lupin continues to strengthen its digital foundation, **running with purpose, growing
with resilience, and innovating without limits.**

We do this to deliver better healthcare outcomes for patients worldwide.

# Alfonso Zulueta

Independent Director

Mr. Zulueta spent over three decades in various roles of increasing responsibility with Eli Lilly
and Company, a global pharmaceutical company, including as Vice President of Global Marketing,
President of Global Oncology and Critical Care Products and most recently, as President of
International responsible for all geographies outside the United States and Canada. He also served
as a corporate officer and member of Eli Lilly and Company’s Executive Committee. Mr. Zulueta
previously served as member of the board of the European Federation of Pharmaceutical Industries and
Associations and the U.S.-Japan Business Council.

Mr. Zulueta currently serves as Non-Executive Chairman of the board of directors of Interpharma
Investments Limited, the holding company of Zuellig Pharma, one of the largest healthcare services
groups in Asia. He is also CEO/Owner of CZ Ventures, LLC, a company focused on start-up investments.
Mr. Zulueta serves as a director of CTS Corporation, a leading global designer and manufacturer of
sensors, actuators and electronic components. He previously served as a director of Amarin
Corporation, Syneos Health, Inc., Calidi Biotherapeutics, Inc., and of Glooko, Inc. Mr. Zulueta
serves on a number of committees of boards including Audit, Compensation and ESG.

[Alfonso Zulueta]

## Education

Economics undergraduate degree from De LA Salle University, Manila, where he was conferred the 2023
Outstanding Alumnus Award.

MBA degree in Marketing/Finance from University of Virginia, USA.

## Committee Membership

Member of the Audit Committee.

Our Leadership

# Dr. Abdelaziz Toumi

CEO – Lupin Manufacturing Solutions

Abdel is a passionate leader with a blend of scientific and commercial skills. He brings over 20
years of experience in the biotech, pharma and CDMO sectors, spanning Europe, North America, and
Asia. Abdel heads Lupin’s API CDMO business, a division that provides custom development and
manufacturing of active pharmaceutical ingredients for clients worldwide.

Abdel joined Lupin from KBI Biopharma, where he led the company’s growth, innovation, and
operational excellence initiatives. He has also held senior roles at Bayer, Merck, Catalent, and
Lonza, where he developed and executed strategies for business development, portfolio expansion, and
customer satisfaction. Abdel has a deep understanding of the global API CDMO industry and its
challenges and opportunities.

He is a six-sigma black belt trainer and has received several awards including the University of
Dortmund PhD award and the Namur Award for Predictive Control of SMB Process.

Abdel holds a Doctorate in Chemical Engineering and an MBA from the University of Southern
Queensland.

# Jeffrey Kindler

Independent Director

Mr. Kindler is an experienced healthcare executive, investor and advisor. He brings over four
decades of business experience and has held leadership positions at some of the world’s most
recognized companies including Pfizer, where he served as Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, as
well as McDonald’s Corporation and General Electric Company. Before that, he was a partner at the
law firm of Williams & Connolly. He is currently CEO of Centrexion Therapeutics, a privately held
biotechnology company, and a Senior Advisor to Blackstone. Mr. Kindler has a deep understanding of
multinational corporate matters including regulations, litigations, compliance, crisis management,
brand, franchise management, executive leadership and mergers & acquisitions.

Mr. Kindler is on the Boards of Precigen Inc., Jazz at Lincoln Center, Perrigo Pharmaceuticals,
Terns Pharmaceuticals, Excision and Entity Risk, Inc. He is Chairman of the Talent & Compensation
Committee of Perrigo Pharmaceuticals; Chairman of the Audit Committee and Member of Compensation
Committee of Precigen Inc.; Chairman of the Compensation Committee of Terns Pharmaceuticals; and a
member of the Audit and Compensation Committees of Jazz at Lincoln Center.

Mr. Kindler is based out of Miami, Florida, USA.

[Jeffrey Kindler]

Bachelor of Arts degree (Summa cum Laude) from Tufts University, USA.

Our Leadership

# K B S Anand

Independent Director

Mr. Anand is well-known for his exceptional business skills and is known for taking balanced risks
with adequate contingency plans. In addition to his customer focus, he is known for his innovative
qualities. Having joined Asian Paints in June 1979, he was appointed as Managing Director & CEO of
Asian Paints in 2012 and he retired in March 2020. Under his leadership, the company’s turnover
increased from 9,600 crores to 19,000 crores. The Forbes Leadership Awards in 2016 recognized Mr.
Anand; and he has served on several leading boards and has extensive experience managing board
dynamics.

[K B S Anand]

## Education

B. Tech (Mech. Engineering) from IIT, Mumbai

PGDM from IIM, Kolkata

## Committee Membership

Chairman of Audit Committee and Stakeholders’ Relationship Committee & Member of the Nomination and
Remuneration Committee and Sustainability and Corporate Social Responsibility Committee.

Our Leadership

# Mark D. McDade

Independent Director

Mr. McDade has had a biopharmaceutical career spanning more than 37 years, where he has held a
progression of COO and CEO roles in complex businesses. He was most recently a lead executive at UCB
Pharma, where he was exceptionally well-regarded and credited with providing steady and resilient
leadership during a time of significant transformation. Mr. McDade has a breadth of experience with
small and large molecule products in a wide range of therapeutic areas, and has a strong track
record of developing, launching, scaling, and managing commercial products. He is the Co-Founder and
Partner at Qiming Venture Partners, USA where since 2017 he has built a strong investment team,
raised three funds and from which numerous high value investments have been made in novel
biotherapeutics, including cell and gene therapy, as well as digital health companies. Mr. McDade is
currently on the Corporate Boards of LetsGetChecked, Inc., Ireland, Talaris Therapeutics, Inc., USA,
Soda Health, USA, as well as the board chair of Icosavax, Inc., USA.

[Mark D. McDade]

## Education

Bachelor of Arts from Dartmouth College, Hanover

MBA from Harvard Business School, Boston

Chairman of Nomination and Remuneration Committee, Member of the Audit Committee, and Risk

# Punita Lal

Independent Director

Punita’s career spans more than 35 years of expertise in strategy, marketing, and leadership
throughout Asia, with experience across varied disciplines, geographies, and cultural contexts. Her
executive experience includes working for Coca Cola in China and PepsiCo in India, where she last
served as MD & CEO of NourishCo, a joint venture between Tata Global Beverages and PepsiCo. After
transitioning from corporate roles, she founded her own consultancy, focusing on the SME sector.
Punita has served on prominent global and Indian boards, including DBS Bank Singapore and Carlsberg
A.S. in Denmark. Additionally, she has held Independent Director roles in India with Cipla Limited,
CEAT Limited, and Entertainment Networks India Limited. As a certified leadership coach and
distinguished business leader, Ms. Lal has earned numerous accolades, such as being named one of
India’s top 20 Businesswomen by Business Today in 2006 and receiving the Corporate Woman of the Year
award in 2009 from the FICCI Women’s Organisation.

[Punita Lal]

## Education

BA(Hons) in Economics from St Stephen’s College, Delhi

MBA from the Indian Institute of Management, Kolkata

## Committee Membership

Member of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and Risk Management Committee.

# Ramesh Swaminathan

Executive Director, Global CFO, Head of IT and API Plus SBU

Ramesh Swaminathan is the Executive Director, Global CFO and Head of IT and API Plus SBU, at Lupin.
A Lord Chevening scholar, Swaminathan is also a qualified Chartered Management Accountant (UK),
Chartered Accountant (India), Company Secretary and a Cost Accountant with more than 30 years of
industry experience, of which 13 years have been with Lupin.

He has also worked with other reputed organisations including VST Industries, SPIC Group, Standard
Chartered Bank, Henkel and L&T.

[Ramesh Swaminathan]

Best CFO by Finance Asia, Best CFO in the pharmaceutical sector by CNBC-TV18, and Business Today
India’s Best CFO for best leverage management – large Indian companies.

# Vinita Gupta

Chief Executive Officer

Vinita Gupta is the CEO of Lupin Limited (Lupin) and Chairperson of Lupin Inc. (LI) and its US
subsidiary, Lupin Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (LPI).

She has not only been responsible for setting up LPI in the U.S and Europe but has also been
instrumental in formulating and executing strategy that has helped Lupin emerge as a global pharma
major. Appointed as the CEO in 2013, it is under her leadership that Lupin has become one of the
largest and fastest growing generics players in the U.S.

Vinita has been regularly named by Forbes Asia in its Top 50 Power Business Women listings for the
Asia Pacific region. Vinita has been widely recognized for her leadership and vision, including the
Business Today Hall of Fame – Most Powerful Women in Business, Outstanding Business Woman Leader of
the Year by CNBC India Business Leader Awards, Forbes India Leadership Awards 2016 Entrepreneur of
the Year, Ernst & Young (EY) Entrepreneur of the Year 2015 as well as the inaugural EY, U.S. 2012
Family Business Award of Excellence and EY Entrepreneur of the Year® 2012 award winner for Health
Services and Technology in Maryland. She is regarded as amongst the most influential Indian Business
Women globally.

[Vinita Gupta]

## Education

A graduate in pharmacy from the University of Mumbai Ms. Gupta also earned her MBA from J L Kellogg
Graduate School of Management.

## Committee Membership

Member of the Sustainability and Corporate Social Responsibility Committee and Risk Management
Committee.

# Nilesh D Gupta

Managing Director

Nilesh Deshbandhu Gupta is a distinguished leader in the pharmaceutical industry and currently
serves as the Managing Director of Lupin. Nilesh joined Lupin in 2002 and has since played a pivotal
role in transforming the company into a global pharmaceutical giant.

Under Nilesh’s visionary leadership, Lupin has expanded its global footprint, entered new markets,
and forged strategic alliances with key industry players. His unwavering commitment to research and
development, coupled with his innovative approach, has led to numerous initiatives to enhance
Lupin's product portfolio, particularly in the areas of generic and specialty pharmaceuticals.

Today, Lupin is a global pharmaceutical leader with products available in over 100 markets. Trusted
by healthcare professionals and consumers, the company has a strong presence in India and the U.S.
across multiple therapy areas. Lupin operates 15 manufacturing sites and 7 research centers
globally.

Nilesh's belief in a patient-centric approach to healthcare is a cornerstone of his leadership at
Lupin. He is committed to improving patient outcomes through innovative and affordable medications.
His vision is to make high-quality healthcare accessible to people worldwide, driving Lupin to
innovate and excel in its offerings continuously.

In addition to his professional achievements, Nilesh is also actively involved in various
philanthropic activities through the Lupin Human Welfare and Research Foundation, contributing to
uplifting the lives and livelihoods of underserved communities.

[Nilesh D Gupta]

## Education

He holds a bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering from the University Department of Chemical
Technology, Mumbai, and an MBA from the Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia.

## Committee Membership

Member of the Sustainability and Corporate Social Responsibility Committee, Stakeholders’
Relationship Committee, and Risk Management Committee.

# Christoph Funke

Chief Technical Operations Officer

Christoph leads Lupin’s global technical operations, overseeing the strategic management of critical
functions including manufacturing, supply chain, and procurement.

With over thirty years of experience in the global pharmaceutical industry, he is known for his
unwavering commitment to innovation and excellence. His career encompasses leadership roles at
Strides Pharma Science and Fresenius Kabi.

Armed with an engineering degree from South Westphalia University of Applied Sciences, Germany,
Christoph brings a wealth of expertise and a proven track record of success to his role.

# Claus Jepsen

President – Global Specialty

Claus Jepsen leads the Global Specialty business at Lupin, with over 30 years of rich experience in
the pharmaceutical industry. He specializes in commercial strategy, portfolio management, and launch
planning across various geographies globally.

Prior to Lupin, Claus was with Takeda Pharmaceuticals and GSK, where he was responsible for strategy
for Rare Diseases, managing franchises in Respiratory and Neurology, and overseeing the launch of
major brands.

Claus holds a Master of Science in Economics and Business Administration from Copenhagen Business
School in Denmark and has pursued further education at IMD in Switzerland and Wharton Business
School in Philadelphia.

Our Leadership

# Dr. Cyrus Karkaria

President – Biotech Businesses

Dr. Cyrus Karkaria leads Lupin’s biotechnology division and is responsible for developing the
company’s global biosimilars portfolio.

With over three decades of experience at Celldex Therapeutics, CuraGen and Biogen, Cyrus has a
proven track record in managing biologic drug development and commercialization of products across
multiple markets, including the U.S.

Cyrus is a post-doctorate from Harvard Medical School and a Ph.D. from the University of Maryland.
He also holds a Master’s degree in biochemistry from Mumbai University.

# Dr. Fabrice Egros

President – Corporate Development

Dr. Fabrice is responsible for driving business in Lupin’s growth markets spanning Latin America and
Asia Pacific. As head of Corporate Development, he drives the strategy and execution of Lupin’s
overall acquisition, business development and licensing plans.

Before joining Lupin, Fabrice has held regional and global roles with industry majors such as UCB,
Sanofi and Pfizer.

He has a doctorate in pharmacy, an MS in drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics, and a Ph.D. in
clinical pharmacology from Paris Saclay, France, apart from a management degree from Harvard
University.

Our Leadership

# Dr. Ranjana Pathak

President - Chief Quality Officer

A seasoned pharmaceutical professional with more than three decades of global experience, Ranjana
brings comprehensive expertise in quality and related functions. She oversees Lupin’s global quality
function.

Ranjana joins us from Dr. Reddy’s, where she was the Global Head for Quality and Pharmacovigilance.
She was a member of the Dr. Reddy’s Management Council and under her leadership, the company
delivered several positive outcomes. Before Dr. Reddy’s, she has held leadership positions in
several branded and generic pharmaceutical companies such as Cipla, Actavis, Endo, Zenith Goldline
and Thames Pharmacal.

Ranjana has a Doctorate in Health Administration from the University of Phoenix, USA, an MBA from
Dowling College, New York, a Post-Graduate Diploma in Pharmaceutical & Chemical Analysis from Sophia
College, Mumbai, and a B.Sc. (Hons) in Chemistry from Mithibai College, Mumbai. She has received
training in leadership in pharmaceuticals and biologics at Harvard University.

# Rajeev Sibal

President – India Region Formulations

Rajeev leads Lupin’s formulations business for the Indian subcontinent and spearheads sales and
marketing for Lupin’s branded generics, trade generics and OTC products. He was also instrumental in
setting up Lupin Diagnostics.

A seasoned pharmaceutical professional with more than three decades of experience, Rajeev has
earlier held leadership positions at Glenmark and Ranbaxy.

Rajeev is a science graduate with certifications from Michigan State University, USA, and Indian
Institute of Management – Ahmedabad and Calcutta, India.

Our supply-integrity promise.

For a buyer who has never met us, the real question is not the price. It is whether the box is what the label says. This is the chain we hold on every single line we ship.

Manufacturer-direct

Every line is sourced straight from a WHO-GMP manufacturer against your purchase order. We are not a broker, we hold no speculative stock, and we do not buy on the grey market.

Documented end to end

A batch Certificate of Analysis, the WHO-format CoPP, the manufacturer's GMP certificate and the cold-chain trail travel with the consignment, prepared to your destination regulator's expectation.

To your licensed entity

We supply the WHO-GMP product; the importer of record is your own licensed local entity. One named desk carries the order from purchase order to the signature on the delivery note.

Rooted in the world's pharmacy

India supplies ~60% of the world's vaccines and the largest share of quality-assured generics outside the US. That is the manufacturing base we buy against, then QA, dossier and ship on your behalf.

Regulator-ready, destination-first

CTD/eCTD dossiers written for MHRA, EMA, SFDA, MoH-UAE, NAFDAC and the rest of the regulators we ship into, not a generic template repurposed page-by-page.

One named person on every order

No call-centre triage, no vanishing reply chains. Your Mumbai desk knows your molecule, your market, your pack-size preference and your customs broker by name.

# From Mumbai to the markets that matter.

M Care was founded in Mumbai in 2003 to solve a single problem: the reliable, regulated-market
supply of essential medicines from India to the hospitals, importers and tender desks that cannot
afford a stock-out. Twenty-plus years on, that is still the only problem we work on.

Who we are

## An export house with a documentation obsession.

We are a privately held pharmaceutical export house with a head office in Mumbai, commercial offices
in London and Dubai, and logistics partners on six continents. Our founding team combined
hospital-side procurement experience with international freight expertise, a blend that still shapes
how we operate.

We're not a broker. We don't buy speculative stock. Every line we ship starts with a purchase order,
runs through a direct manufacturer relationship, and ends with a signature on a delivery note.
That's the short version of why importers, hospital pharmacies and tender desks trust us with repeat
business for years at a time.

We sell from Mumbai into 49+ markets across ten regions: the UK, Germany and France in Europe; UAE,
Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and Bahrain across the GCC; Türkiye, Jordan, Iraq, Yemen, Egypt,
Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia across the wider MENA and Maghreb; Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa,
Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, Mauritius, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, Cameroon, DR Congo and
Mozambique across the African continent; Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bangladesh in South Asia; the
Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia in ASEAN; Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan in Central Asia;
Azerbaijan in the Caucasus; Ukraine across Eastern Europe through donor and ProZorro channels; and
Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, Peru, Chile and the Dominican Republic in Latin America and the Caribbean.
India, where our head office sits, is deliberately not one of those markets. We are a pharmaceutical
*exporter*, not an Indian domestic supplier.

Quality & compliance

## The documentation defines the deal.

Our entire value proposition rests on documentation that survives an audit. Every manufacturing
partner is qualified against a standard protocol, WHO-GMP as the baseline, EU-GMP or US-FDA where
the destination market demands it. Every batch ships with a full certificate of analysis, method of
analysis, certificate of origin, and pack insert matched to the destination label.
* **Quality standards:** WHO-GMP is the baseline; EU-GMP / US-FDA / PIC/S partners for regulated
markets.
* **Certifications:** ISO 9001:2015 for the export operation. ISO 13485 partnerships for medical
devices.
* **Regulatory reach:** CTD/eCTD dossiers for MHRA, EMA, SFDA, DHA, MOHAP, NAFDAC, PPB, TFDA,
SAHPRA, and the Gulf Health Council.
* **Artwork control:** destination-market labelling reviewed and locked *before* shipment, with
change-control discipline on every revision.
* **Cold-chain:** audited 2–8°C and −25°C lanes with validated temperature loggers on every unit;
excursion protocol insured and written into the PO.

What we don't do

## A business defined as much by what we turn down.

Pharmaceutical exports is a trade where the sharp edges are obvious. Ours is a simple list.

### No grey-market stock

Every batch is traceable to a single manufacturing site, with a paper chain that would hold up in
any regulator's audit. We don't resell parallel-imported or secondary-market stock.

### No counterfeits, no compromises

Every partner site is physically audited by our QA team before first order and re-audited on a
defined cycle. Non-compliant partners are removed from the roster, no exceptions, ever.

### No surprise pricing

Your quote includes insurance, freight, dossier, and artwork. No invoice bloat after the shipment
ships. What you confirm on day one is what you pay on day forty.

## Pharmaceutical exports

The core of the business: finished-formulation pharmaceuticals supplied against hospital, retail
chain, distributor and tender orders. Oncology, anti-infectives, cardiovascular, CNS, diabetes,
gastroenterology and respiratory portfolios, every line traceable to a single WHO-GMP or EU-GMP
manufacturing site.
* Direct manufacturer purchase, no broker stock, no batch mysteries, no parallel-import exposure.
* CTD/eCTD dossiers for first-time registrations; variation management and renewals for existing
licences.
* Destination-market artwork locked before despatch, with change control on every revision.
* Batch-level documentation on every shipment: CoA, MoA, certificate of origin, pack insert.

Pillar 02

## Cold-chain & biologicals

Vaccines, insulins, monoclonal antibodies, blood-derived products, IVF hormones, the molecules that
fail without a temperature-controlled chain. Our cold-chain protocol is the single most-audited part
of our business because it's the most-asked-about part.
* Validated 2–8°C and −25°C lanes with real-time temperature telemetry on every consignment.
* Pre-cleared freight lanes with DHL Life Sciences, Kuehne+Nagel Pharma, and regional specialist
couriers.
* Airport-to-customs excursion escalation protocol, written, rehearsed, insured.
* Full cold-chain documentation pack: pre-shipment temperature validation, in-transit logs,
on-arrival inspection record.

**Independent QP release** available where destination-market regulation requires it.

## Unlicensed & named-patient imports

When a prescribed medicine isn't licensed in the destination market, or a licensed product is on

compassionate-use supply, turnaround measured in days, not weeks.
* MHRA Specials for the UK; EMA Article 5(1) compassionate-use frameworks; GHC / SFDA / DHA
named-patient pathways for the Gulf.
* Same-day response on named-patient enquiries during working hours; out-of-hours on-call for
emergency cases.
* Dedicated unlicensed-imports desk with hospital-pharmacy experience, we speak your language.
* Full import documentation package, including prescriber justification template.

## Oncology supply lives or dies on the shortage list, and we plan for the shortage list, not the
## launch list.

Hospital pharmacy buyers in the UK and EU know the shortage rhythm. Docetaxel ran short in 2024–25,
bortezomib in 2024, paclitaxel periodically since 2019. The MHRA's Drug Shortage Notification
Programme and the FDA's Drug Shortage list converge on the same finished-dose lines, and the gap is
typically not raw API but finished-dose manufacturing capacity. That is exactly what an Indian
WHO-GMP supplier closes, within a 5- to 14-day window when the named-patient route under Regulation
167 or an EU Article 5 unlicensed-medicines pathway is invoked. Our oncology catalogue is sized for
shortage response, not for retail reorder.

On the Gulf side, NUPCO and the Saudi Ministry of Health Central Drug Store run two-yearly oncology
tenders covering the Reserve cytotoxics (paclitaxel, docetaxel, gemcitabine, oxaliplatin,
carboplatin, cisplatin, pemetrexed) and the targeted therapies (bortezomib, capecitabine). The
dossier load is heavy, Arabic-language SmPC, Saudi-domestic stability, batch-specific CoA
cross-referenced to GHC central registration. We carry the supply-side document pack pre-built so a
tender response goes from RFI to bid in days, not weeks.

On the African side, oncology procurement runs through CHAI's cancer programmes, Global Fund Pooled
Procurement Mechanism (PPM) for HIV-associated lymphoma protocols, and direct ministry-of-health
buying through KEMSA, MSD Tanzania and Central Medical Stores Ghana. WHO prequalification on the
supplier and the manufacturer is the entry ticket; a CoPP from CDSCO and a recent on-site GMP audit
close the loop. Nine molecule pages below carry the full clinical and regulatory context buyers need
before a quote enters the procurement pipeline.

## AMR, Reserve antibiotics and the procurement lane we actually run.

Anti-infectives are the tender line that buyers cannot afford to get wrong. The WHO Global
Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance System attributes an estimated 1.27 million deaths a year to
bacterial AMR, the hardest-hit regions being sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, which are also where
most of our tender volume lands. Stewardship is the policy; supply continuity is the precondition
for any policy to work.

The WHO AWaRe classification splits antibiotics into Access, Watch and Reserve tiers. Our catalogue
sits mostly in the first two (amoxicillin, cefixime, ceftriaxone, azithromycin), with Reserve agents
(meropenem, imipenem-cilastatin, linezolid, fosfomycin IV) supplied against specialist hospital and
teaching-hospital demand where a carbapenem-sparing strategy still needs a carbapenem on the shelf.
Every Reserve SKU ships with a batch-specific CoA, destination-language stability data and the
regulator-approved pack insert, not a best-effort translation.

Antifungals (fluconazole, itraconazole, amphotericin B liposomal, voriconazole) and antiparasitics
(albendazole, praziquantel, artemether-lumefantrine, pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine) cover the
tropical-medicine lane, where WHO prequalification and NAFDAC, PPB or TMDA registration matter more
than GCC-style SFDA dossiers. We carry both dossier routes against the same molecule where demand is
split. 1,870 lines across 60 molecules, sized for a government tender or a single ward pack.

## NCDs are now 74% of global mortality. Cardiovascular is where the tender spend is.

Cardiovascular medicines are the backbone of ministry-level non-communicable-disease programmes. WHO
puts NCDs at roughly 74% of global deaths, with cardiovascular disease alone accounting for about
17.9 million deaths a year, most of them in low- and middle-income countries where hypertension
treatment coverage still sits below 30%. The procurement implications are prosaic: statins, ACE
inhibitors, ARBs, beta-blockers and antiplatelets drive a large share of a public hospital's
pharmacy budget, and tenders run annually.

On our roster, the workhorses are atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, amlodipine, telmisartan, ramipril,
bisoprolol, carvedilol and clopidogrel, all WHO Essential Medicines List entries, all available in
the dosage ladder a hospital formulary actually needs (5 / 10 / 20 / 40 mg strengths; tablets and
combination products where the destination market has approved them). Anticoagulants (warfarin,
apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, low-molecular-weight heparins) ship with the cold-chain
validation the destination regulator expects where applicable.

The rarer lines, sacubitril/valsartan for heart failure, ivabradine for sinus-rhythm rate control,
PCSK9 inhibitors where local tender specifies them, go through the same dossier discipline as the
high-volume generics. 1,407 lines across 60 molecules. GCC central registration, MHRA named-patient,
BfArM §72 AMG import or NAFDAC / PPB / SAHPRA national registration, we run all four lanes.

## WHO mhGAP: most mental-health patients in LMICs are untreated. Supply is part of why.

Central nervous system medicines are the thinnest formulary in most low- and middle-income
countries. WHO's Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) has documented treatment coverage for
severe mental disorders below 25% in many LMIC settings, with epilepsy treatment coverage frequently
below 50%. The causes are many; reliable supply of off-patent essentials is one we can actually fix.

The antiepileptic workhorses, phenytoin, carbamazepine, sodium valproate, levetiracetam,
lamotrigine, clonazepam, are all on the WHO Essential Medicines List and all on our roster, in the
tablet, capsule, oral-solution and injectable formats a neurology ward actually needs. Antipsychotic
supply is dominated by haloperidol, chlorpromazine, risperidone, olanzapine and quetiapine; our
[risperidone][19] spoke covers the tablet, oro-dispersible and long-acting depot presentations.
Antidepressants (sertraline, fluoxetine, escitalopram, amitriptyline, mirtazapine) and anxiolytics
(diazepam, lorazepam, alprazolam) ship with the controlled-drug licensing paperwork the destination
narcotics authority requires.

Parkinsonian, neuropathic-pain and multiple-sclerosis lines sit alongside: levodopa-carbidopa,
pregabalin, gabapentin, duloxetine, baclofen, and the higher-complexity disease-modifiers where a
CTD dossier is the price of entry. 1,311 lines across 60 molecules. The tender desk gets one
supplier for the whole category, not five.

## 537 million people with diabetes, and the cold-chain lane that serves them.

Diabetes is the fastest-growing non-communicable disease of the decade. The IDF Diabetes Atlas puts
global prevalence at 537 million adults in 2021, rising to an estimated 783 million by 2045, with
the sharpest rates of increase across the Middle East, North Africa, sub-Saharan Africa and
Southeast Asia, our primary export lanes. Insulin access, metformin continuity and oral-antidiabetic
breadth are the three things a ministry programme depends on, and all three are
manufacturing-and-logistics problems before they are clinical ones.

Our insulin lines (human insulin regular and NPH, glargine, lispro, aspart, detemir, degludec,
premix 30/70 and 70/30 presentations) ship under 2–8°C validated cold-chain with continuous logger
data handed over at destination. The WHO Prequalification programme has added biosimilar insulins to
its list; we source from prequalified and GMP-audited origin where the tender specifies it. Oral
antidiabetics, metformin, glimepiride, gliclazide, vildagliptin, sitagliptin, empagliflozin,
dapagliflozin, ship at ambient.

Thyroid (levothyroxine, carbimazole, methimazole), adrenal (hydrocortisone, prednisolone,
dexamethasone) and bone-metabolism lines (alendronate, risedronate, zoledronic acid, calcitriol)
round out the endocrine shelf. 471 lines across 60 molecules. One supplier, one dossier trail, one
cold-chain process, for the whole endocrine programme.

## Antivirals, the WHO-PQ catalogue, donor-funded HIV programmes, and the Hepatitis C generic that
## quietly closed a treatment gap.

Antiretroviral therapy (ART) procurement under the Global Fund and PEPFAR is the single largest
pooled HIV-medicine market in the world, and Indian generic manufacturers have held more than 80% of
the WHO-prequalified ART supply for over a decade. Tenofovir / lamivudine / dolutegravir (TLD) is
now the WHO-recommended first-line regimen for adults; TAF-based regimens are second-line.
Paediatric formulations (abacavir-lamivudine + dolutegravir-10mg, raltegravir granules) are
smaller-volume but harder to source. Our antivirals catalogue carries the full first-line and
second-line ART list against WHO PQ status, with the dossier ready for Global Fund Pooled
Procurement Mechanism (PPM), national HIV programme tenders (Nigeria's NACA, Kenya's NASCOP, South
Africa's national ART tender) and PEPFAR direct buying.

Hepatitis C direct-acting antivirals (sofosbuvir, sofosbuvir-velpatasvir, sofosbuvir-daclatasvir,
glecaprevir-pibrentasvir) transformed the disease from chronic to curable in 8–12 weeks. Indian
generic versions under the original Gilead and AbbVie voluntary licensing arrangements made the
per-treatment cost workable for low- and middle-income countries, exactly the price point hospital
pharmacy buyers in Egypt's national HCV elimination programme, the Pakistan Punjab HCV programme,
and the Africa CDC HCV co-infection lane all needed. We carry the dossier pack for both donor-funded
and direct-buyer windows.

Outside HIV and HCV, the antivirals catalogue carries the influenza neuraminidase inhibitors
(oseltamivir, zanamivir), CMV antivirals (ganciclovir, valganciclovir) for transplant procurement,
and the COVID-era residual (remdesivir, molnupiravir, nirmatrelvir-ritonavir) where national
stockpile re-orders are still active. Compliance routes vary, WHO PQ where the molecule is on the
list, NAFDAC / PPB / SAHPRA registration for African direct-buy markets, MHRA Specials for UK
shortage management on niche antivirals.
